Optro is focused on a triad of key factors: audit, risk, and compliance management. This AI tools’ primary focus? Automating time-intensive workflows and sharing smart recommendations. ### 2. Workiva – Best for using Gen AI for financial and ESG reporting

Workiva is a cloud-based data management system for compliance and reporting. In particular, you’ll want to turn to its Generative AI for ESG, financial reporting, audit, and risk management purposes alike. The AI also assists in drafting, summarizing, and refining financial and non-financial reports, ensuring consistent tone and high-quality outputs tailored to specific needs. [...] PersefoniAI users praise its “AI-friendly approach” to carbon measurement and reporting but what stands out is the Persefoni Copilot that answers technical questions related to carbon accounting through a chat-like interface.

Persefoni AI further supports businesses with anomaly detections and identifying errors in their Scope 1-2-3 emissions data. You can consider the platform if you want to comply with the most notable carbon accounting standards, including IFRS S2, CSRD, and the SBTi.

However, this platform primarily focuses on carbon footprint management, (unlike other more comprehensive ESG reporting software on the market). So the AI for ESG capabilities are also somewhat limited to what the platform can do and are influenced by the tool’s occasional shortcomings.

Despite enterprise leaders' best efforts, persistent sustainability challenges exist. These include fragmented data sources, manual reporting inefficiencies, unreliable external inputs and greenwashing risks. In short, challenges exist throughout the lifecycle -- from data collection and reporting to validation and assurance.

AI tools can help automate ESG data collection and aggregation, and improve data integrity by detecting inconsistencies and streamlining the compliance process.

results.title: Will AI Change ESG Reporting? An Honest Assessment
results.content:
Ultimately, while AI has shown promise in automating certain aspects of ESG reporting, we should stay grounded in reality.

I think most criticism of applications of AI comes from a place of holding excessive expectations. And some of this excessive expectation is actually the fault of misleading marketing tactics, depicting the smallest AI feature as the must-have, all-encompassing solution to your ESG needs.

As best practices, definitions, and even regulations around ESG reporting evolve before our eyes, AI-powered software needs to be flexible enough to adapt to a fund’s or a company’s specific ESG requirements. Out-of-the-box AI tools will not be the panacea to all the problems and roadblocks your ESG team currently faces.
